Temporary removal of a portion of the sidewalk is therefore proposed to establish adequate construction access. Work includes saw-cutting and removing the affected concrete sidewalk, excavating to expose the wall, preparing the substrate, installing waterproofing and a protective layer, backfilling and compacting, and reconstructing the sidewalk to City-approved grades and standards. Temporary barricades, pedestrian access provisions, and excavation support will be provided as required. Work limits, excavation depth, and duration will be shown on the proposed site plan for City review. No permanent encroachment or reduction in sidewalk width is proposed.

TRAILSIDE Project Description Project Overview Trailside is a proposed residential community located on approximately 13.86 acres in the City of Newport Beach, representing one of the City’s last remaining infill development opportunities of significant scale. The property occupies a distinctive location at the northern end of Upper Newport Bay, on a portion of the existing Newport Beach Golf Course, and offers the opportunity to create a new residential neighborhood alongside extensive publicly accessible recreational open space and connections to the regional trail network. The property is within the Airport Area subarea of the City’s Housing Element and is the only designated housing site in that subarea located within the boundaries of the Newport-Mesa Unified School District. The site is generally bounded by Mesa Drive to the north, Irvine Avenue to the west, Delhi Channel to the south, and Santa Ana Heights to the east. The approximately 13.86-acre project site is currently envisioned to include approximately 8.45 acres for residential development, approximately 3.94 acres for the biological buffer required under the City's Local Coastal Program, and approximately 1.47 acres reserved for anticipated dedication to the County of Orange in connection with its Delhi Channel expansion project. The biological buffer is also anticipated to be dedicated to the City of Newport Beach for permanent public open space and recreational opportunities. The final acreage allocations will be refined through the planning, engineering, and entitlement process. Together, these elements would transform a portion of the existing fee-based golf course into a residential community with substantial new public recreational opportunities. Residential Development The residential component is planned on approximately 8.45 acres and is anticipated to consist of approximately 175 for-sale homes in three distinct product types: three-story detached single-family residences, three-story attached townhomes, and four-story attached townhomes. The mix of product types is intended to offer a range of home designs and sizes within a cohesive, thoughtfully landscaped community. The neighborhood will feature landscaped internal streets, pedestrian connections, and convenient access to the adjoining public recreational corridor. An on-site affordable housing component is also contemplated, currently estimated at approximately 5% to 10% of the residences, with the final program and income levels to be determined during entitlement review. Private Community Amenities Trailside is envisioned as an amenity-rich residential neighborhood with a resort-style swimming pool, fitness center, sports court, outdoor barbecue facilities, and landscaped gathering areas. Internal pedestrian connections will link these amenities and provide multiple connections to the adjoining public recreational open space and regional trail system. Controlled-access vehicle gates are also contemplated at residential entrances for nighttime security. The proposed gate configuration and operating hours will be subject to City and Coastal Commission review, with public access maintained during established public-use hours. Public Recreational Open Space and Trail Connectivity A defining feature of Trailside is the proposed creation of approximately 3.94 acres of publicly accessible recreational open space within the Delhi Channel biological buffer corridor required under the City's Local Coastal Program. This area is included within the overall project site but is contemplated separately from the residential development area and is anticipated to be dedicated to the City of Newport Beach for permanent public open space and recreational use. The buffer responds to the anticipated Delhi Channel expansion and the environmentally sensitive habitat area (ESHA) associated with the improved channel. Unlike the existing golf course, which requires payment to play and primarily serves golfers, the proposed public recreational amenities would be available free of charge and offer activities that can be enjoyed by people of all ages and interests, including those who do not golf. Conceptual public amenities include a pickleball court, volleyball court, fitness trail, expansive lawn areas, outdoor barbecue facilities, landscaped gathering places, passive open-space areas, and a multiuse trail. These features are intended to establish an inviting linear recreational destination for residents and the broader Newport Beach community. Their final locations and configurations will be designed to respect the applicable biological-buffer requirements and remain subject to agency review. The multiuse trail is anticipated to extend along the project site and connect to the existing Upper Newport Bay regional trail network, while also serving as a County of Orange maintenance access road. The trail is expected to consist primarily of decomposed granite, with limited asphalt or concrete surfaces where appropriate. No lighting is proposed along the public trail or within the biological buffer. Public use is contemplated during established daytime and early-evening hours, generally coordinated with the surrounding OC Parks trail system, subject to regulatory approval. Five dedicated on-site public parking spaces are proposed to complement existing public parking in the surrounding area. Delhi Channel and Coastal Resource Protection The project is being coordinated with the County of Orange's planned Delhi Channel widening and improvement project. The current conceptual plan identifies approximately 1.47 acres for anticipated dedication to the County of Orange for channel improvements, approximately 3.94 acres for the biological buffer and anticipated dedication to the City of Newport Beach, and approximately 8.45 acres for residential development. These areas remain subject to refinement as the project advances through the entitlement process. The conceptual plan addresses a 100-foot biological buffer measured from the applicable environmentally sensitive habitat area (ESHA) limits associated with the improved Delhi Channel. The initial 50 feet are proposed primarily for passive uses, including the multiuse trail, native landscaping, and landscaped slopes. The additional buffer area is proposed to accommodate compatible public recreational amenities and gathering areas, consistent with the applicable Local Coastal Program framework and subject to agency confirmation. The project team is coordinating with City of Newport Beach and California Coastal Commission staff regarding buffer treatments, public-access provisions, and the required functional equivalency analysis. The intent is to demonstrate meaningful improvements in public recreational access relative to the existing golf course use while protecting adjacent habitat resources. Site Access and Infrastructure Improvements Trailside will incorporate new residential access, internal circulation, landscaping, pedestrian connections, and supporting utility infrastructure. The conceptual plan includes access from Mesa Drive and related intersection and circulation improvements, subject to further engineering and City review. Infrastructure planning will be coordinated with the County’s Delhi Channel improvements, including the public multiuse trail and maintenance access. These investments are intended to improve connectivity along the northern Upper Newport Bay corridor while supporting the proposed residential neighborhood. Project Vision Trailside represents an uncommon opportunity to deliver approximately 175 new for-sale homes on an 8.45-acre residential development area within the largely built-out City of Newport Beach. Its combination of private community amenities, approximately 3.94 acres of public recreational open space anticipated for dedication to the City, direct trail connectivity, and a separate 1.47-acre area set aside for anticipated dedication to the County for channel expansion distinguishes the project from a conventional infill residential development. By transforming a fee-based recreational use into free, publicly accessible amenities that serve a broader range of interests and abilities, while improving access to the Upper Newport Bay trail system, Trailside is envisioned to create enduring value for future residents and the broader Newport Beach community.
